title: ADR: Feature Toggle Contract and Safe Rollout
author: Maya Patel
content:
Status
------
Published decision record. This ADR defines the contract for feature toggles (feature flags) exposed through Redwood services' APIs and the safe rollout / rollback semantics enforced by runtime and infra systems. It standardizes naming, types, server/client behavior, observability requirements, and operational runbooks.

Context and motivation
----------------------
Feature toggles are widely used across Redwood to control experimentation, staged rollouts, emergency mitigations, and progressive exposure of behavior (e.g., kernel selection, quantization mode, routing policy toggles, or new API fields). In the last 18 months we observed incidents where loose toggle semantics caused:
- Silent divergences between client and server expectations (clients sending flags that older backends ignored but still changed routing)
- Unsafe rollouts that bypassed SLO guardrails and caused customer-facing errors
- Poor observability for flag-driven regressions (no signal tying a SLI change to a toggle)

We need a minimal, consistent contract that:
- Prevents backward/forward compatibility mismatches between clients and servers
- Makes rollouts observably tied to SLOs and traceable to owners
- Enables safe automatic rollback and staged rollout policies enforced at the infra level

Decision summary
----------------
We adopt a single, typed feature-toggle contract across the platform, enforced by the API gateway and runtime sidecars. Key choices:
1) Feature flags are first-class, typed fields in the RPC/HTTP contract (see API section). Flags are namespaced and versioned.
2) The runtime provides a deterministic precedence: request-level toggle -> tenant-level toggle -> global default.
3) Toggle evaluation must be idempotent and side-effect free. No toggle should change request routing semantics in a way that alters trace IDs or request identity.
4) All toggles require an owner, intent, and an observable metric delta plan before canary rollout.
5) Gatekeepers (gateway + rollout service) will enforce canary percentage, SLO thresholds, and automatic rollback when thresholds are breached.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- Any RPC/HTTP input that toggles behavior of inference or control-plane logic (model selection, quantization mode, KV cache bypass, routing tier).
- Infrastructure rollout tooling: console rollouts, API-based rollouts, and CLI-driven emergency toggles.
Excludes: purely client-side UI feature flags that do not change server-side inference or billing behavior.

API contract
------------
Clients must express flags in a typed flags envelope. For JSON REST and gRPC the canonical representation is:

- REST (example JSON payload snippet):
  {
    "input": "Generate an email",
    "flags": {
      "x:inference.quantize_mode": "fp16",     // string enum
      "x:inference.prefetch": false,            // boolean
      "x:route.override_pool": "cpu-small"    // string
    }
  }

- gRPC: equivalent map<string, string> with typed hint header: X-Flag-Types: key1=enum,key2=bool

Rules:
- Flag names MUST be namespaced with a stable prefix (x:inference., x:runtime., x:billing.)
- Types supported: boolean, enum (string), integer, percentage (0-100).
- Servers MUST validate types and reject requests with unknown types (400) if the request indicates "strict":true in the flags envelope.
- Default behavior: if a client omits a flag, runtime falls back to tenant->global default chain; servers must NOT silently interpret unknown flag names as true.

Flag lifecycle & naming
-----------------------
- Naming convention: <domain>.<component>.<short-action> (examples: x:inference.quantize_mode, x:runtime.kv_cache_bypass)
- Creation: flags are created in the rollout service catalog with metadata: owner, description, allowed values, safety checklist, observability plan, and blocking SLOs.
- Deprecation: flags older than 6 months without active use are reviewed quarterly and either migrated to defaults or removed with a deprecation header and 3-month client notice.

Flag types and semantics
-----------------------
Table: flag configuration fields (plain text table)
- name: stable identifier
- type: boolean|enum|int|pct
- default: global default value
- allowed_values: comma-separated (for enum)
- owner: team name
- canary_policy: {percent, duration} (expressed via rollout metadata)
- slo_guard: comma-separated SLIs to monitor (latency_p50, error_rate_5m)

Runtime precedence and determinism
--------------------------------
Evaluation order for any request: request-level flags > tenant-specific flags > environment (region) flags > global default.
Rules:
1) Deterministic evaluation: for percentage flags use RFC-6234-compatible hash(service, tenant_id, request_id) mod 100 to assign bucket so repeated retries land in same bucket.
2) Evaluation must be computed in the sidecar/gateway to avoid differences between intra-service calls.
3) No flag may alter the canonical request ID or sampling decision; side effects must be recorded separately.

Observability requirements
-------------------------
Every rollout MUST include the following observability plan before canary:
- Primary SLIs: p50 latency, p95 latency, error_rate_5m, cost_per_token_1h
- Instrumentation: toggle-eval span tag (flag.name=VALUE), rollout-id tag, tenant-id, and owner tag on root trace.
- Dashboards: one per rollout showing SLI deltas vs baseline and by-tenant breakdown.
- Alerts: automated alert when error_rate_5m increases by > 0.5% absolute or p95 latency increases by > 50ms sustained for 5 minutes.

SLO interaction and automatic rollback
------------------------------------
- Each rollout registers a guard: a set of SLO thresholds. If a guard is tripped, the rollout service will trigger automated rollback to the previous stable bucket and open an incident with the owner team.
- Rollback thresholds are configurable per rollout but must meet a minimum safety baseline: error_rate_5m delta <= +0.5% and p95 delta <= +100ms.

Operational runbook (canary rollout)
-----------------------------------
1) Create flag in rollout catalog and link owner/team and observability plan.
2) Deploy server-side support (if required) behind feature-checks and add tests (unit + integration).
3) Start rollout at 1% for 15 minutes. Observe SLIs.
4) If no guard is tripped, increase to 5% for 30 minutes.
5) Continue to 25% for 1 hour, then 50% for 2 hours, then 100% if stable.
6) If a guard trips at any stage, automated rollback to prior percentage and page owner via pager duty.

Emergency toggle flow
---------------------
- CLI: `redwood toggle set <name> --tenant <id> --value false --emergency` triggers global immediate set and creates audit entry. Only users in the emergency escalation group (security, infra, SRE) can perform emergency toggles.
- Emergency toggles bypass canary but still write audit logs and trigger immediate SLI evaluation.

Security and audit
------------------
- All flag changes are audited (who, what, when, rollout-id).
- Access control: flags with billing or privacy impact require "restricted" permission; console will hide these to non-authorized users.

Developer guidance and testing
-----------------------------
- Unit tests: flags must be asserted in both true and false branches; for enums test all allowed values or a representative sample.
- Integration tests: include a deterministic percentage seed so test requests land consistently in/out of percentage buckets.
- Contract tests: a lightweight client-side verifier that asserts server responds with 400 when strict=true and flag types mismatch. Add to preflight CI job.

Alternatives considered
----------------------
1) Unstructured free-form flag headers (REJECTED): simpler but caused silent mismatches and poor discoverability.
2) Client-side-only flags (REJECTED for server-behavior toggles): lacks centralized control and observability.
3) Full per-tenant remote config service for every decision (REJECTED for now due to latency and operational cost; may revisit for very high-frequency decisions).

Consequences and follow-ups
--------------------------
- Positives: predictable rollouts, tighter coupling between flags and observability, and automatic defense against regressions.
- Work required: rollout of sidecar/gateway validation logic, adoption of rollout catalog, and adding preflight contract tests.
- Migration: existing ad-hoc flags must be cataloged and assigned owners within 90 days. Legacy toggles will be mapped to the new namespaced names as a compatibility layer.

Implementation plan and milestones
--------------------------------
- Q1 2026: Implement gatekeeper validation in API Gateway and sidecars. Launch rollout catalog MVP. Begin onboarding two pilot services (model-router and caching).
- Q2 2026: Expand to all inference-facing services and require rollout metadata for new flags. Start quarterly deprecation review.
- Q3 2026: Enforce strict flag validation by default in SDKs and client libraries.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Flag catalog: infra-rollout team (owner: Rita Gómez)
- API/gateway enforcement: runtime team (owner: Ethan Zhang)
- Observability integration: platform-observability (owner: Liam O'Connor)

References and related policies
------------------------------
- See rollout service README in infra docs for API examples and CLI references.
- Related: service-dependency-isolation-and-runtime-feature-gating-standards-2026 (architectural guidance)

Appendix: example rollout catalog entry (YAML)
--------------------------------------------
name: x:inference.quantize_mode
type: enum
allowed_values: [none, fp16, int8-q4]
default: none
owners: [team:runtime, owner:maya.patel@redwood.com]
canary_policy:
  steps: [{percent:1,duration_minutes:15},{percent:5,duration_minutes:30},{percent:25,duration_minutes:60}]
slo_guard: [error_rate_5m:0.5,p95_delta_ms:100]

CLI examples
------------
- Create flag: `redwood rollout create --file quantize_mode.yaml`
- Start rollout: `redwood rollout start --name x:inference.quantize_mode --tenant default`
- Emergency off: `redwood toggle set x:inference.quantize_mode --tenant all --value none --emergency`

This ADR will be revisited if the rollout catalog requires changes or after the first three pilot rollouts complete.
